messages:
Tanya (Support): FYI ACME reported a sharp drop in embeddings throughput this morning. Tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec collapsed ~10x. No 5xx in logs, customer sees 200s but queuing and long tail latency.

Mike (Infra): Any chance this is an auth/billing 429 causing retries? or a batch-window change?

Tanya (Support): We checked billing: no rate limit spikes and their requests are succeeding. They reported vector dim mismatch error earlier but that was a separate customer payload issue and fixed. This seems platform-side: high GPU queue depth, vector pipeline saturation.

Sanjay (ML Eng): Can you paste a sample request + timestamps (first/last) and a short span of our internal metrics? I want tokens/sec vs vectors/sec, kvcache hit rate, and gpu_util.

Tanya (Support): Sample from customer (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-768","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"]}'
```
Times: first seen 4620000450, last failure spike 4620001080

Tanya (Support): Metrics snippet around 4620001000:
```
vectors/sec: 18
tokens/sec: 720
gpu_util: 97%
kvcache_hit: 0.12
queue_depth: 126
avg_batch_size: 1.3
```

Mike (Infra): GPU saturation + small batch sizes -> likely continuous batching breakdown. Avg_batch_size 1.3 is the killer. We recently rolled out an autosplit heuristic tweak at 4620000700 that lowered max wait for tiny requests. DeployBot: can you confirm deploys?

DeployBot: Canary deploy "autosplit-v2" to runtime-pool-a completed at 4620000698 by mike_infra. No rollback recorded.

Anna (DevEx): That autosplit heuristic change was intended to reduce latency for small requests; side-effect can hurt throughput for high qps mixed token/vector workloads. If tokens/sec is steady but vectors/sec down, small batchers might be evicting vector-ready work because of dim checks.

Sanjay (ML Eng): Hypothesis: autosplit causes early flush for tiny token requests, starving vector batches that require larger aggregation for kernel efficiency. With high gpu_util we see queuing; throughput for vectors collapses because kernels aren't fed optimal batch dims.

Tanya (Support): Customer timeline aligns: degradation started ~4620000800 right after canary ramp. They run mixed token+embed traffic.

Mike (Infra): Quick repro plan: 1) Synthetic mixed workload locally: 90% small token gen (seq len 8), 10% embedding requests (dim 768) at same overall request rate. 2) Toggle autosplit wait window from 8ms -> 40ms. 3) Observe avg_batch_size, queue_depth, vectors/sec.

Sanjay (ML Eng): Repro steps I ran on staging (commands):
```
# generate mixed traffic
python tools/mixload.py --token-rate 900 --embed-rate 100 --token-len 8 --embed-batch-preference random --duration 300
# toggle autosplit
rccli set runtime.autosplit.wait_ms 8  --pool staging
rccli set runtime.autosplit.wait_ms 40 --pool staging
```

Sanjay (ML Eng): Results (staging):
```
autosplit.wait_ms=8  -> vectors/sec 22, tokens/sec 900, avg_batch_size=1.4, gpu_util=95, queue_depth=110
autosplit.wait_ms=40 -> vectors/sec 310, tokens/sec 880, avg_batch_size=8.9, gpu_util=88, queue_depth=18
```

Anna (DevEx): Strong signal. Short wait window breaks batching for embeddings. Also saw kvcache_hit very low in the bad config — likely because batches didn't aggregate repeated prefixes.

Mike (Infra): Immediate mitigation options: 
- Roll back autosplit-v2 on canary and pause global rollout (fast).
- Increase autosplit wait_ms for runtime pools serving mixed workloads.
- Add traffic-class isolation so embedding requests have separate batching queues.

Tanya (Support): Customer needs ETA. Which is fastest?

Mike (Infra): Fastest is rollback canary -> should restore prior behavior in minutes. I'll open a rollback and link here.

DeployBot: Rollback request created: rollback-autosplit-v2 by Mike (4620001120). Action queued to runtime-pool-a.

Sanjay (ML Eng): Also adding a short smoke test we can run post-rollback: run mixload for 60s and assert vectors/sec > 250 and avg_batch_size > 6. I'll add to runtime test harness.

Anna (DevEx): For longer term, we should tune autosplit heuristics to consider request type and avg sequence lengths; maybe have per-model wait_ms. Filing a follow-up RFC.

Tanya (Support): I'll update ACME: rollback initiated, asking them to confirm when they see recovery. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Mike (Infra): Monitoring alert rule updated to watch vector_token_gap (tokens/sec / max(1,vectors/sec)) > 20 for 3min.

Tanya (Support): ACME confirmed partial recovery at 4620001135. They reported vectors/sec back to ~290 and latencies normalized. Closing for now but keeping ticket open until autosplit rollout is gated.

Anna (DevEx): Noted action items: RFC + per-model wait config + add embed-specific batching queue.

Sanjay (ML Eng): I'll send the staging test logs + exact rccli commands to the ticket.

Tanya (Support): Thanks everyone.
